El Nino and La Nina Global Temperature Anomalies

Source: R/SquareR-package.R
el_nino.Rd

Global dataset outlining the magnitude and direction of the temperature shift, or anomaly that changes in oceanic currents cause, which is dubbed El Nino when the shift is positive, and La Nina when negative.

data(el_nino)

Format

A data frame with 920 rows of 5 variables:

Entity

Area under the affect of the temperature anomaly

Code

ID code for Entity

Month

Date in YYYY-MM format

Temperature anomaly

Difference of a specific month's average surface temperature from the 1991-2020 mean, in degrees Celsius

Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) anomaly

A measure of the sea surface temperature anomalies in the east-central tropical Pacific Ocean

Source

Temperature anomaly: Copernicus Climate Change Service Information ERA5

Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) anomaly: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

Data processing: Our World in Data

Examples

  summary(el_nino)
#>        Entity           Code           Month     Temperature anomaly
#>  Length   :920   Length   :920   Length   :920   Min.   :-1.06003   
#>  N.unique :  1   N.unique :  1   N.unique :920   1st Qu.:-0.59373   
#>  N.blank  :  0   N.blank  :  0   N.blank  :  0   Median :-0.33131   
#>  Min.nchar:  5   Min.nchar:  8   Min.nchar:  7   Mean   :-0.26067   
#>  Max.nchar:  5   Max.nchar:  8   Max.nchar:  7   3rd Qu.: 0.03084   
#>                                                  Max.   : 0.93061   
#>  Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) anomaly
#>  Min.   :-2.04000                
#>  1st Qu.:-0.51000                
#>  Median :-0.04000                
#>  Mean   : 0.02098                
#>  3rd Qu.: 0.50000                
#>  Max.   : 2.59000                
  Temperature_anomaly <- el_nino$`Temperature anomaly`
